note: Fresh questions modelled on KSEAB-style skills and mark levels; not copied from historical papers.

questions.question: Why did Lencho have complete faith that God would help him after the hailstorm?
answer_points: His crop was destroyed and he was desperate.
He believed God could see his suffering and would help him.

questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: How does Mandela distinguish personal freedom from the freedom of his people?
answer_points: He explains that individual freedom was restricted by apartheid.
He came to understand that his people also needed political and social freedom.
His struggle therefore became a collective struggle.

questions.question: What made the young seagull finally overcome his fear of flying?
answer_points: Hunger made him move towards the food offered by his mother.
He discovered that his wings could support him when he jumped.

questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: Why did Anne decide that writing in a diary would help her despite having loving people around her?
answer_points: She felt that she lacked a true friend with whom she could share her deepest thoughts.
A diary could listen without judging her.
Writing helped her express and understand her feelings.

questions.question: Why is the baker an important part of traditional Goan life?
answer_points: Bread was closely connected with daily life and celebrations.
The baker and his bread were part of a long-standing Portuguese-Goan tradition.

questions.question: Describe two ways in which Mijbil showed intelligence and curiosity.
answer_points: He explored objects and discovered ways of playing with them.
He learned to use water and household objects creatively.
His behaviour showed adaptability and curiosity.

questions.question: What does Valli's careful planning of the bus journey reveal about her personality?
answer_points: She is observant and determined.
She gathers information and plans carefully before acting.

questions.question: How did Kisa Gotami's understanding of death change during her search for mustard seeds?
answer_points: She initially believed her own loss was unique.
Meeting other families showed her that death comes to every household.
She gradually accepted the universality of death.

questions.question: How does the quarrelling between Lomov, Natalya and Chubukov create humour in The Proposal?
answer_points: The characters turn a marriage proposal into arguments over property and dogs.
They behave irrationally over trivial matters.
Their exaggerated pride and anger create comic situations.
The contrast between the purpose of the visit and their behaviour makes the play humorous.

questions.question: How does the natural incident in Dust of Snow change the poet's mood?
answer_points: The falling snow shakes him out of a negative mood.
It makes him feel that part of the day has been saved.

questions.question: Why are fire and ice suitable symbols for the destructive forces discussed in the poem?
answer_points: Fire represents desire or uncontrolled passion.
Ice represents hatred or emotional coldness.
Both can destroy human relationships and the world.

questions.question: Contrast the tiger's life in the zoo with the life he should naturally have in the jungle.
answer_points: In the zoo he is confined and frustrated.
In the jungle he would move freely and hunt naturally.
The poem highlights the cruelty of captivity.

questions.question: How does humour make the dangerous animals in the poem less frightening to the reader?
answer_points: The poet uses exaggerated and playful descriptions.
Dangerous encounters are presented as comic instructions.

questions.question: What lesson about loss does the boy begin to learn in The Ball Poem?
answer_points: He experiences the pain of losing something he values.
He begins to understand that loss is part of life.
He must learn to cope with loss rather than expect everything to be replaced.

questions.question: Why does Amanda repeatedly imagine different worlds while being addressed by the speaker?
answer_points: She wants to escape constant instructions and criticism.
Her fantasies provide freedom and peace.
They reveal her desire for independence.

questions.question: Mention two qualities of animals that the poet admires in contrast to human beings.
answer_points: Animals are contented and free from excessive desire.
They are not obsessed with possessions or social status.

questions.question: What can the movement of the trees towards the forest symbolise?
answer_points: It can symbolise the desire for freedom.
The trees appear to resist confinement indoors.
Their movement suggests a return to their natural environment.

questions.question: Why does the poet compare the fog to a cat?
answer_points: Both arrive quietly and silently.
The fog seems to move and settle with the quiet, watchful quality of a cat.

questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: How does Custard prove that appearances can be misleading?
answer_points: He is mocked as cowardly by the other animals.
When the pirate arrives, Custard alone acts decisively.
His actions prove him to be genuinely brave.

questions.question: Lencho's faith is strong but also ironic. Explain.
answer_points: He sincerely believes that God will help him after the crop is destroyed.
He receives money through the post office employees.
Instead of appreciating their help, he suspects the post office workers of stealing part of God's money.
This creates irony because the people he mistrusts are actually the ones who help him.
